title: Skeletal & muscular systems in sport
examples: What is the difference between a hinge joint and a ball and socket joint?
How do muscles work together to make me kick a football?
Can you explain how the bones help support my body?

explain.say: The skeleton gives your body its shape and support.
Bones protect your soft and vital internal organs.
Joints allow your bones to move smoothly when you play sport.
Muscles pull on bones to create movement in your joints.
The biceps and triceps are a common muscle pair for bending the arm.
When you bend your elbow, the biceps contracts and pulls the forearm bones.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a ligament and a tendon?
faq.a: A ligament connects bone to bone, keeping joints stable. A tendon connects muscle to bone, allowing movement.
asks: Is it the same as a muscle?
What keeps my joints from popping apart?

faq.q: Do all joints allow the same types of movement?
faq.a: No, joints are specialized. For example, the hip joint allows movement in many directions, unlike the elbow.
asks: Can I move my wrist like my hip?
What limits how much I can bend?

faq.q: How does muscle contraction actually cause movement?
faq.a: Muscles work in pairs. When one muscle contracts, it pulls the bone, and the opposing muscle must relax to allow the movement.
asks: What happens when I try to lift something heavy?

faq.q: Are the bones always rigid, or can they change?
faq.a: Bones are hard, but they are constantly remodeling themselves. This process makes them strong enough for the stresses of sport.
asks: Do bones get stronger with exercise?
Can bones break and fix themselves?

faq.q: What is the function of the rib cage specifically?
faq.a: The rib cage's main function is to protect the delicate organs inside your chest, like your heart and lungs.
asks: What is the rib cage protecting?
Are the ribs just for show?

facts: The skeleton provides the framework for the body.
Joints allow for specific, controlled movements.
Muscles work in antagonistic pairs to create movement.
Ligaments connect bone to bone for stability.

quiz.say: Which structure connects muscle to bone, allowing movement?
quiz.why: A tendon is specifically designed to attach muscle force to bone.

wrong.1: Ligaments connect bone to bone, not muscle to bone.
wrong.2: Bone is the rigid structure that is being moved, not the connector.
wrong.3: Muscle is the source of the force, but the tendon is the attachment point.

quiz.say: The shoulder joint allows movement in many directions. What type of joint is this?
quiz.why: The ball and socket joint allows the greatest range of motion, like the shoulder.

wrong.0: Pivot joints only allow rotation around one axis, like a doorknob.
wrong.1: Gliding joints allow only slight sliding movements between bones.
wrong.3: Hinge joints only allow movement in one plane, like a door.

quiz.say: If the bicep contracts to bend the elbow, what must happen to the tricep?
quiz.why: Muscles work in opposition; one must relax for the other to pull effectively.

wrong.0: Movement requires coordinated action between opposing muscle groups.
wrong.2: If both contracted hard, they would pull against each other, causing no movement.
wrong.3: Stretching is passive; the relaxation is the active requirement for movement.
